intro: A Funktionsverbgefüge (FVG, noun-verb construction) splits a verb into a noun that carries the meaning and a 'light' verb that carries tense, person and aspect: anwenden → zur Anwendung kommen, erwägen → in Erwägung ziehen, ausdrücken → zum Ausdruck bringen. Official, legal and academic German prefer them because the noun can take attributes (scharfe Kritik üben) and because the light verb adds nuance: bringen/stellen are active and causative (etwas zur Sprache bringen, etwas zur Verfügung stellen), kommen/stehen/treten are passive or stative (zur Anwendung kommen, zur Verfügung stehen, in Kraft treten). The noun and its preposition are fixed, so you learn them as chunks; the light verb then behaves like any verb: it is conjugated at position 2, sent to the end in a subordinate clause, turned into a participle in the perfect (hat zum Ausdruck gebracht, ist in Kraft getreten) and placed after zu in an infinitive clause (zum Abschluss zu bringen).
tips[0].title: Active or passive: the light verb decides
tips[0].text: bringen, stellen, nehmen, ziehen = someone acts on something. kommen, stehen, treten, gelangen = something happens or is the case. The same noun can take both.
tips[0].check.why: The reading room itself is the subject (ein neuer Lesesaal), so you need the stative verb: zur Verfügung stehen. stellen would need someone who provides it.
tips[1].title: The light verb moves, the noun stays
tips[1].text: Like a separable prefix, the noun phrase stays at the end of the main clause; the light verb is conjugated at position 2, goes to the end in a subordinate clause and forms the perfect with its own auxiliary.
tips[1].trap: in Kraft treten forms its perfect with sein (ist in Kraft getreten), unter Beweis stellen with haben (hat unter Beweis gestellt): the auxiliary belongs to the light verb.
tips[1].check.why: The auxiliary belongs to the light verb, and treten forms its perfect with sein: ist in Kraft getreten.
tips[2].title: Fixed prepositions after the chunk
tips[2].text: Many FVGs govern a preposition of their own: Bezug nehmen auf + Akk, Kritik üben an + Dat, Rücksicht nehmen auf + Akk, Abstand nehmen von + Dat.
tips[2].check.why: The chunk is Kritik üben an + dative; the preposition is fixed and must be learned with it.
tips[3].title: Register lift in a formal e-mail
tips[3].text: In a formal e-mail one or two FVGs raise the register at once; too many make the text stiff. Keep them for the key actions: reference, request, decision.
tips[3].check.why: One construction for the key action (the reference) lifts the register; stacking several makes the text stiff, and none at all sounds too casual.
table.caption: Funktionsverbgefüge of written German
remember[0]: bringen / stellen / nehmen / ziehen = active; kommen / stehen / treten = passive or stative.
remember[1]: Only the light verb is conjugated; the noun chunk stays at the end of the clause.
remember[2]: Learn the chunk with its preposition: Bezug nehmen auf, Kritik üben an, Abstand nehmen von.
mistakes[0].why: treten is a verb of motion and forms its perfect with sein.
mistakes[1].why: Being available is stative (stehen); stellen needs an object that is provided.
mistakes[3].why: English make a decision; German uses treffen (formally also fällen).
hook: Learn 'zur Verfügung stellen', 'in Kraft treten' and friends as chunks, and your formal writing gains the weight of official German.
